stories.title: Former aircraft engineer’s garden rooms firm opens £500,000 showroom site near Penyffordd
stories.summary: A garden rooms company has opened a £500,000 showroom site on a former farmyard near Penyffordd. Rubicon Garden Rooms said sales have risen by about 25 per cent since it moved from Deeside Enterprise Centre in Shotton. stories.title: Safety fears fail to halt Saltney school merger as plans move to final stage
stories.summary: A consultation on plans to merge two Saltney primary schools has entered the final stage of public engagement despite huge opposition from both schools. stories.title: ‘Gathering dust’: Labour MS presses Welsh Government on A55 and A494 studies
stories.summary: Studies into how to make the A55 and A494 safer and more reliable will be published in full when they are ready, the Welsh Government’s deputy transport minister has said. Mark Hooper was responding in the Senedd on Tuesday after a statement on Wales’s roads that covered the Menai crossings and the M4 around Newport.

stories.title: Catholic school closures in Flintshire move to 28-day objection period after Cabinet vote
stories.summary: Flintshire County Council’s Cabinet has voted to press on with plans to close four Catholic schools and build a £55m school in Flint for pupils aged three to 18. stories.title: Offices in China or flood defences in Broughton: the question put to the First Minister
stories.summary: The First Minister has defended Welsh Government spending on overseas offices after being asked how he could tell flooded residents in Flintshire the money was better spent abroad. Rhun ap Iorwerth was questioned on the offices at First Minister’s Questions, where two opposition MSs argued the money should go on public services and flood defences
